title: 1963 AHSME Problem 14
statement: Given the equations \(x^2+kx+6=0\) and \(x^2-kx+6=0.\) If, when the roots of the equations are suitably listed, each root of the second equation is \(5\) more than the corresponding root of the first equation, then \(k\) equals:

solutions.text:
The first pair of roots has sum \(-k,\) while the second has sum \(k.\) Since both roots increase by \(5,\) \(k=-k+10,\) so \(k=5.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Compare the sums of the two pairs of roots
Adding \(5\) to each root increases their sum by \(10\)
